ch0.s2.text: Texting with a dictionary open gives you time to think, but not to explain yourself. So: this.
ch0.s3.text: I'm Jorginho. In Mexico, people call me Jorge, Jorch, or Yorch, depending on how well they know me. I code, study, and play several instruments.

ch1.s1.title: A normal day
ch1.s2.text: First thing: a workout. Running, swimming, the gym, or cycling. I'm kind of a David Goggins... just saying.
ch1.s3.text: Then: work. I build websites, I like IoT, and I placed third at a hackathon. Unfortunately (or fortunately) I'm into nerdy things. One thing I have as a non-negotiable: I don't work outside of office hours.
ch1.s4.text: Then: study. I'm in school and practice cello when I can. Sometimes the two overlap.
ch1.s5.text: This year I'm training for a marathon. The half marathons were the rehearsal.
ch1.s6.text: Sometimes dinner is canned tuna with banana and avocado. I also eat kiwi with the skin on.

ch2.s1.title: Music
ch2.s2.text: In order: drums, guitar, piano, cello. I taught myself almost all of them. The cello demands more attention. The piano still wins.
ch2.s3.text: Playing in public makes me nervous. I also like that part.
ch2.s4.text: Once, at a concert, I tried a stick trick, hit the cymbal, and got silence.
ch2.s5.text: A couple of things that did get recorded.

ch3.s1.title: China
ch3.s2.text: I lived in Wuhan and studied Chinese at HUST for about five or six months. Then came Furongzhen, Beijing, Chongqing, Guangzhou, and Zhangjiajie.
ch3.s3.text: Coming back from Guangzhou to Wuhan, we missed our train because we lingered over pizza at an Italian place. It wasn't even that good.
ch3.s4.text: We caught another train, bought new tickets within about fifteen minutes, and told no one out of embarrassment.
ch3.s5.text: On Chinese trains, people snored. We'd arrive complaining that we hadn't slept. I made it to HSK 1.

ch4.s2.text: Three statements. One is a lie.

ch4.reveal.text: The lie is number three: I'm training for a marathon, but I haven't run a full one yet.
ch5.s1.title: Adrenaline
ch5.s2.text: In Zhangjiajie I did one of the highest bungee jumps in the world. My body did not want to jump.
ch5.s3.text: In Puerto Vallarta, around June 2025, I went skydiving from a small plane. The ground slowly pulled away and, when the door opened, there was nothing there.
ch5.paracaidas.label: SKYDIVE · PUERTO VALLARTA · JUN 2025 (APPROX.)
ch5.s4.text: The instructor said: “Get your feet out, but don't put them anywhere. Just let them dangle.” Horrible. I'd do it again.
ch5.s5.text: I climbed Nevado de Colima without once wanting to quit.

ch6.s1.title: My people
ch6.s2.text: Elian listens to my bad jokes with a patience that should count as a sport by now.
ch6.s3.text: At home there are two ferrets, a turtle, a chihuahua, a cat, and a little bird. The ferrets bite my ankles when they go outside.
ch6.s4.text: I like laughing with friends and doing things together. I like showing up. I want people to know they've got a shoulder to lean on.

ch7.s4.title: Food
ch7.s4.text: I love farofa. Mexico has chilaquiles, sotol, and carne seca, all worth trying. Sushi keeps showing up.
ch7.s5.text: Right now I'm planning a trip to Brazil: São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro. The itinerary already has more personality than I do.

ch8.s1.title: What's next
ch8.s2.text: Remote work: more room to travel, build websites, and make things like a Raspberry Pi BMO.
ch8.s3.text: An Ironman. The goal sounds ambitious, which is exactly why it stays written down.
ch8.s4.text: More languages. Portuguese comes with a dictionary and conjugation tables.
ch8.s5.text: After that: Armenia, Pakistan, the Middle East, Russia, and more of Latin America. The list is in no hurry.

ella.title: Things I know about you
ella.lede: It's a short list. I'd rather admit that than make up the rest.
ella.zh.caption: You speak Chinese. HSK level: 1,000,000.
ella.item1: Chinese is common ground. Mine stopped at HSK 1, after five or six months in Wuhan.
ella.item2: Gabi says we have the same sense of humor... I think so. A bold claim: now I have to live up to it.
ella.item3: You write in Portuguese. I reply with the dictionary open. I suspect I'm losing.
ella.q1: How did you end up speaking Chinese?
ella.q2: Which place in Brazil should I see first?
ella.q3: What makes you laugh the hardest?
